stem:
Amara wants to read at least 18 books this year. She has already read 7 books. What is the minimum number of additional books Amara must read to meet her goal?
A. 7
B. 11
C. 18
D. 25
type: T1 — word problem, minimum additional amount to reach a goal (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Easy — one subtraction step: 18 − 7 = 11

distractor_rationales.A: Student reported the books already read rather than the additional books needed
distractor_rationales.C: Student reported the total goal rather than the additional amount needed
distractor_rationales.D: Student added the goal and books already read (18 + 7 = 25) instead of subtracting

stem:
A student needs a minimum of 120 community service hours to graduate. The student has already completed 74 hours. What is the minimum number of additional hours the student must complete to graduate?
A. 46
B. 52
C. 74
D. 194
type: T1 — word problem, minimum additional hours to meet a requirement (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Easy — 120 − 74 = 46; one subtraction step

distractor_rationales.B: Student subtracted from an incorrect reference value rather than from the 120-hour requirement
distractor_rationales.C: Student reported the hours already completed rather than the additional hours needed
distractor_rationales.D: Student added the requirement and hours completed (120 + 74 = 194) instead of subtracting

stem:
A farmer needs at least 45 pounds of fertilizer to treat a field. The farmer already has 37 pounds. What is the minimum number of additional pounds of fertilizer the farmer needs?
A. 37
B. 8
C. 45
D. 82
type: T1 — word problem, minimum additional supply to meet a need (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Easy — 45 − 37 = 8; one subtraction step

distractor_rationales.A: Student reported the amount already on hand rather than the additional amount needed
distractor_rationales.C: Student reported the total requirement rather than the additional amount needed
distractor_rationales.D: Student added the requirement and the amount on hand (45 + 37 = 82) instead of subtracting

stem:
A greenhouse requires a minimum temperature of 72°F to grow tropical plants. The current temperature is 65.5°F. What is the minimum number of degrees the temperature must increase?
A. 2.5
B. 6.5
C. 7.5
D. 8.5
type: T1 — word problem, minimum increase to meet a temperature threshold (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: minimum number of degrees ... must increase
why_this_difficulty: Easy — 72 − 65.5 = 6.5; one decimal subtraction

distractor_rationales.A: Student subtracted from an incorrect current value rather than finding the gap to the threshold
distractor_rationales.C: Student used 73 as the threshold instead of 72 (73 − 65.5 = 7.5)
distractor_rationales.D: Student used 74 as the threshold instead of 72 (74 − 65.5 = 8.5)

stem:
A fundraiser has a goal of raising no more than $5,000. The fundraiser has already collected $3,218. What is the maximum additional amount, in dollars, the fundraiser can collect while staying within the goal?
A. 1,782
B. 3,218
C. 5,000
D. 8,218
type: T1 — word problem, maximum additional amount under a cap (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Easy — 5,000 − 3,218 = 1,782; one subtraction step

distractor_rationales.B: Student reported the amount already collected rather than the remaining allowance
distractor_rationales.C: Student reported the total cap rather than the maximum additional amount
distractor_rationales.D: Student added the cap and the amount already collected (5,000 + 3,218 = 8,218)

stem: A school needs at least 75 chairs for an event. Chairs are sold in packs of 8. What is the minimum number of packs that must be ordered?
type: T1 — word problem, minimum packs to cover a need when partial packs are not sold (SPR)
why_this_difficulty: Easy — 75 ÷ 8 = 9.375; since partial packs cannot be ordered, round up to 10

stem:
According to a survey, adults sleep a minimum of 5 hours and a maximum of 9 hours per night. Which inequality represents all possible values of the number of hours h an adult sleeps per night, based on this survey?
A. h ≥ 14
B. h ≤ 5
C. 5 ≤ h ≤ 9
D. h ≥ 9
type: T2 — compound inequality from stated minimum and maximum (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality represents all possible values of
why_this_difficulty: Easy — two endpoints given directly; form a ≤ h ≤ b

distractor_rationales.A: Student added the two bounds (5 + 9 = 14) and wrote it as a lower limit
distractor_rationales.B: Student used only the lower bound and applied it as an upper bound (wrong direction)
distractor_rationales.D: Student used only the upper bound and wrote it as a lower bound (wrong direction)

stem:
A cyclist's speed on a trail varies between 8 miles per hour and 14 miles per hour. Which inequality best represents this situation, where s is the cyclist's speed, in miles per hour?
A. s ≤ 6
B. s ≤ 8
C. s ≤ 14
D. 8 ≤ s ≤ 14
type: T2 — compound inequality directly from a stated range (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality best represents this situation
why_this_difficulty: Easy — both bounds given; translate 'between 8 and 14' directly to 8 ≤ s ≤ 14

distractor_rationales.A: Student subtracted the two bounds (14 − 8 = 6) and used the result as a single upper bound
distractor_rationales.B: Student used only the lower bound and applied it as an upper bound
distractor_rationales.C: Student used only the upper bound, omitting the lower bound entirely

stem:
A chemist estimates that the volume of a liquid sample is greater than 3.5 liters but less than 6.0 liters. The liquid weighs 1.2 kilograms per liter. Which inequality represents this situation, where w represents the estimated total weight, in kilograms, of the liquid sample?
A. 1.2 − 6.0 < w < 1.2 − 3.5
B. 1.2 + 3.5 < w < 1.2 + 6.0
C. 1.2(3.5) < w < 1.2(6.0)
D. 1.2/6.0 < w < 1.2/3.5
type: T2 — compound inequality requiring multiplication of a unit rate by a volume range (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Easy — multiply the unit weight (1.2) by each volume bound; recognize multiplication, not addition

distractor_rationales.A: Student subtracted each volume bound from the unit weight instead of multiplying
distractor_rationales.B: Student added each volume bound to the unit weight instead of multiplying
distractor_rationales.D: Student divided the unit weight by each bound instead of multiplying

stem:
During a laboratory experiment, the temperature of a solution ranged between 18°C and 26°C. Which inequality best represents this situation, where t is the temperature, in degrees Celsius, of the solution during the experiment?
A. t ≤ 8
B. t ≤ 18
C. t ≤ 26
D. 18 ≤ t ≤ 26
type: T2 — compound inequality directly from a stated temperature range (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality best represents this situation
why_this_difficulty: Easy — both bounds stated directly; translate 'between 18 and 26' to 18 ≤ t ≤ 26

distractor_rationales.A: Student found the range (26 − 18 = 8) and wrote it as a single upper bound
distractor_rationales.B: Student used only the lower bound and applied it as an upper bound
distractor_rationales.C: Student used only the upper bound, omitting the lower bound entirely

stem:
A florist can arrange at most 30 bouquets per day. The florist makes rose bouquets and lily bouquets. Which inequality represents this situation, where r is the number of rose bouquets and l is the number of lily bouquets the florist makes in one day?
A. r + l ≤ 30
B. r + l ≥ 30
C. r − l ≤ 30
D. r − l ≥ 30
type: T3 — write two-variable inequality from a total-capacity constraint (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: where r is ... and l is
why_this_difficulty: Easy — direct translation of 'at most 30 total' into r + l ≤ 30

distractor_rationales.B: Student reversed 'at most' to 'at least', writing ≥ instead of ≤
distractor_rationales.C: Student used r − l instead of r + l, subtracting the counts rather than adding
distractor_rationales.D: Student subtracted the variables and reversed the inequality direction

stem:
Marcus and Elena are painting rooms. Marcus paints at a rate of 2 rooms per hour and Elena paints at a rate of 3 rooms per hour. Together they painted fewer than 36 rooms in one day. Which inequality represents this situation, where m is the number of hours Marcus painted and e is the number of hours Elena painted?
A. 2m + 3e > 36
B. 2m + 3e < 36
C. 3m + 2e > 36
D. 3m + 2e < 36
type: T3 — write two-variable inequality matching each rate to the correct person (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: where m is ... and e is
why_this_difficulty: Easy — multiply each person's rate by their hours; 'fewer than 36' gives strict <

distractor_rationales.A: Student formed the correct expression but reversed 'fewer than' to 'greater than'
distractor_rationales.C: Student swapped the rates, assigning 3 to Marcus and 2 to Elena, and reversed the direction
distractor_rationales.D: Student swapped the rates but kept the correct inequality direction

stem:
Priya has $20 to spend on notebooks and pens. Each notebook costs $3.50 and each pen costs $1.25. Which inequality represents the relationship between the number of notebooks n and the number of pens p Priya can buy?
A. 3.50n + 1.25p ≤ 20
B. 3.50n + 1.25p ≥ 20
C. 1.25n + 3.50p ≤ 20
D. 1.25n + 3.50p ≥ 20
type: T3 — write two-variable budget inequality (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality represents the relationship between
where n is ... and p is
why_this_difficulty: Easy — total cost = 3.50n + 1.25p must not exceed $20

distractor_rationales.B: Student reversed the budget direction, writing ≥ instead of ≤
distractor_rationales.C: Student swapped the prices of notebooks and pens
distractor_rationales.D: Student swapped the prices and reversed the inequality direction

stem:
A parking garage charges a $6 entrance fee plus $4 per hour. A driver wants to spend at most $30 on parking. Which inequality represents this situation, where h is the number of hours the driver parks?
A. 4h ≤ 30
B. 4 + 6h ≤ 30
C. 6h ≤ 30
D. 6 + 4h ≤ 30
type: T3 — write one-variable inequality for a fixed-fee-plus-hourly-rate scenario (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: charges a $ entrance fee plus $ per hour
why_this_difficulty: Easy — total = 6 (flat) + 4h (hourly) ≤ 30; identify the correct structure

distractor_rationales.A: Student wrote only the hourly component without including the flat entrance fee
distractor_rationales.B: Student swapped the flat fee and the hourly rate (4 + 6h instead of 6 + 4h)
distractor_rationales.C: Student wrote only the flat fee multiplied by h, omitting the per-hour rate

stem:
The point (5, 3) in the xy-plane is a solution to which of the following systems of inequalities?
A. x > 0
   y > 0
B. x > 0
   y < 0
C. x < 0
   y > 0
D. x < 0
   y < 0
type: T7 — identify the system of inequalities satisfied by a given point (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: is a solution to which of the following systems of inequalities
why_this_difficulty: Easy — both coordinates are positive; substitute 5 and 3; only x > 0 and y > 0 is satisfied

distractor_rationales.B: Student correctly identified x > 0 (since 5 > 0) but incorrectly wrote y < 0 despite 3 > 0
distractor_rationales.C: Student reversed the sign for x, writing x < 0 even though 5 > 0
distractor_rationales.D: Student reversed the signs of both coordinates

stem:
A model estimates that the wind speed during a storm was at least 25 miles per hour and at most 55 miles per hour. Which inequality represents the possible values of the wind speed w, in miles per hour, during the storm?
A. w ≥ 80
B. w ≥ 55
C. 0 ≤ w ≤ 25
D. 25 ≤ w ≤ 55
type: T2 — compound inequality from 'at least' and 'at most' bounds (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality represents the possible values of
why_this_difficulty: Medium — must correctly apply both 'at least' (≥) and 'at most' (≤) to form a compound inequality

distractor_rationales.A: Student added the two bounds (25 + 55 = 80) and used the sum as a single lower bound
distractor_rationales.B: Student used only the upper bound and wrote it as a lower bound (reversed direction)
distractor_rationales.C: Student used 0 as the lower bound and the actual minimum (25) as the upper bound

stem:
A model estimates that a honeybee colony produces between 40 and 60 pounds of honey per year. Based on this model, which inequality represents the estimated total pounds of honey, p, that 12 colonies could produce in one year?
A. 40 + 12 ≤ p ≤ 60 + 12
B. (40)(12) ≤ p ≤ (60)(12)
C. 40 ≤ 12 + p ≤ 60
D. 40 ≤ 12p ≤ 60
type: T2 — compound inequality requiring multiplication of a per-unit range by the number of units (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality represents the estimated total
why_this_difficulty: Medium — total = per-colony range × number of colonies; must multiply both bounds by 12, not add

distractor_rationales.A: Student added 12 to each bound instead of multiplying
distractor_rationales.C: Student added p to 12 inside the bounds, treating the per-colony limits as total limits
distractor_rationales.D: Student placed 12p inside the original per-colony range as if scaling the variable, not the bounds

stem:
A biologist classifies a fish species as large if its typical adult length is more than 30 centimeters. Each of the following inequalities represents possible lengths l, in centimeters, for a specific fish species. Which inequality represents possible lengths for a large fish species?
A. 34 < l < 52
B. 15 < l < 30
C. 8 < l < 24
D. 10 < l < 29
type: T2 — select the compound inequality consistent with a stated minimum threshold (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality represents possible lengths for a large fish species
why_this_difficulty: Medium — a large fish has length > 30; must identify which range has ALL values exceeding 30

distractor_rationales.B: Represents lengths of 15–30 cm; the upper endpoint reaches but does not exceed 30 cm
distractor_rationales.C: Represents lengths of 8–24 cm; all values are well below the 30 cm threshold
distractor_rationales.D: Represents lengths of 10–29 cm; all values are below the 30 cm threshold

stem:
The width of a rectangle is 12 meters and the length is x meters. The perimeter of the rectangle is at most 80 meters. Which inequality represents this situation?
A. 2x + 24 ≤ 80
B. 2x + 24 ≥ 80
C. 2x + 12 ≤ 80
D. 2x + 12 ≥ 80
type: T3 — write a one-variable inequality for a perimeter constraint (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Medium — perimeter = 2(12) + 2x = 24 + 2x; must apply 'at most' as ≤

distractor_rationales.B: Student reversed 'at most' to ≥ instead of ≤
distractor_rationales.C: Student computed 12 + 2x instead of 2(12) + 2x, adding the width only once
distractor_rationales.D: Student used the wrong perimeter formula and reversed the inequality direction

stem:
A conference room holds no more than 50 people total, consisting of seated and standing attendees. The number of seated attendees must be at least twice the number of standing attendees. Which system of inequalities represents this situation, where a is the number of seated attendees and b is the number of standing attendees?
A. a + b ≤ 50 and a ≥ 2b
B. a + b ≥ 50 and a ≤ 2b
C. a + b ≥ 50 and a ≥ 2b
D. a + b ≤ 50 and a ≤ 2b
type: T3 — write a system of two-variable inequalities from a two-constraint scenario (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which system of inequalities represents this situation
why_this_difficulty: Medium — two constraints: 'no more than 50' means ≤, and 'at least twice' means ≥

distractor_rationales.B: Student reversed the first constraint to ≥ and also reversed the seated/standing ratio to ≤
distractor_rationales.C: Student reversed the first constraint to ≥ but correctly wrote a ≥ 2b
distractor_rationales.D: Student correctly wrote the total ≤ 50 but reversed the ratio constraint to a ≤ 2b

stem:
A delivery van can carry a maximum of 2,800 pounds. During one trip, the van will carry a 300-pound piece of furniture along with x small boxes weighing 15 pounds each and y large boxes weighing 40 pounds each. Which inequality represents the possible combinations of small boxes, x, and large boxes, y, the van can carry in one trip?
A. 15x + 40y ≤ 2,500
B. 15x + 40y ≥ 2,500
C. 40x + 15y ≤ 2,800
D. 40x + 15y ≥ 2,800
type: T3 — write two-variable inequality for combined weight after subtracting a fixed load (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality represents the possible combinations
why_this_difficulty: Medium — subtract the fixed furniture weight (2,800 − 300 = 2,500) to find available capacity; assign weights to correct variables

distractor_rationales.B: Student correctly found 2,500 for box capacity but reversed the direction to ≥
distractor_rationales.C: Student swapped the weights for small and large boxes and used the gross capacity (2,800) without subtracting the furniture
distractor_rationales.D: Student swapped the box weights and reversed the inequality direction

stem:
A cargo truck can carry no more than 3,200 pounds per trip. The cargo container weighs 850 pounds, and each package weighs 65 pounds. What is the maximum number of packages that can be loaded for one trip?
A. 36
B. 37
C. 40
D. 41
type: T4 — solve for maximum quantity given a fixed-plus-variable weight constraint (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Medium — set up 850 + 65x ≤ 3,200; solve x ≤ 36.15; floor to 36 since partial packages are not allowed

distractor_rationales.B: Student solved correctly to 36.15 but rounded up to 37, which would exceed the weight limit
distractor_rationales.C: Student divided the total capacity by package weight without subtracting the container weight first (3,200 ÷ 65 ≈ 49.2... wait that's not 40)
distractor_rationales.D: Student divided the total capacity by the package weight and rounded up, ignoring the container weight

stem: A community center charges a $50 rental fee plus $8 per participant. A club has a budget of $250 for the event. What is the greatest number of participants the club can have?
type: T4 — word problem, solve for maximum participants under a total budget (SPR)
sat_key_phrases: charges a $ rental fee plus $ per participant
why_this_difficulty: Medium — set up 50 + 8x ≤ 250; solve x ≤ 25; exact integer answer

stem: A company produces custom T-shirts for a flat setup fee of $60 plus $14 per shirt. The company has a budget of $340 to spend on T-shirts for an event. What is the greatest number of T-shirts the company can order?
type: T4 — word problem, solve for maximum quantity under a total budget (SPR)
why_this_difficulty: Medium — set up 60 + 14x ≤ 340; solve x ≤ 20; exact integer answer

stem:
y < −5x + 10
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given inequality?
A. (−3, 0)
B. (0, 11)
C. (2, 0)
D. (3, 0)
type: T5 — which ordered pair satisfies a linear inequality? (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which point (x, y) is a solution to the given inequality
why_this_difficulty: Medium — must substitute each pair; the large negative x-value in choice A creates a high right-hand side (25) that y easily satisfies

distractor_rationales.B: Substituting (0, 11): 11 < −5(0) + 10 = 10 is false
distractor_rationales.C: Substituting (2, 0): 0 < −5(2) + 10 = 0 is false — equality does not satisfy the strict inequality
distractor_rationales.D: Substituting (3, 0): 0 < −5(3) + 10 = −5 is false

stem: x is at most 8 less than 4 times y. If y = 5, what is the greatest possible value of x?
type: T6 — interpret a two-variable bound and find max x for a given y (SPR)
why_this_difficulty: Medium — translate 'x is at most 8 less than 4y' to x ≤ 4y − 8; substitute y = 5 to get x ≤ 12

stem:
The maximum value of x is 6 more than 5 times another number m. Which inequality shows the possible values of x?
A. x ≥ 5m + 6
B. x ≤ 5m + 6
C. x ≥ 6 − 5m
D. x ≤ 6 − 5m
type: T6 — translate a verbal two-variable bound into an inequality (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Medium — 'maximum of x is 5m + 6' means x ≤ 5m + 6; 'maximum' signals ≤, not ≥

distractor_rationales.A: Student correctly computed 5m + 6 but wrote ≥, treating 'maximum' as if it were 'minimum'
distractor_rationales.C: Student reversed the order in the expression (6 − 5m) and used ≥
distractor_rationales.D: Student reversed the order in the expression (6 − 5m) but used ≤

stem:
y > 8
2x + y < 24
The point (x, 35) is a solution to the system of inequalities above. Which of the following could be the value of x?
A. −6
B. −5
C. 3
D. 7
type: T7 — find the value of x that satisfies a system when y is given (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: is a solution to the system of inequalities
which of the following could be the value of x
why_this_difficulty: Medium — y = 35 satisfies y > 8 automatically; substitute into 2x + 35 < 24 to get x < −5.5; only −6 qualifies

distractor_rationales.B: Student found x < −5.5 correctly but selected −5, which does not satisfy x < −5.5
distractor_rationales.C: Student reversed the inequality direction, solving 2x + 35 > 24 instead
distractor_rationales.D: Student solved 2x + y = 24 using y = 8 rather than y = 35, finding the wrong boundary

stem:
y > 3x + 5
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
A. x: 1, 3, 5 | y: 9, 15, 21
B. x: 1, 3, 5 | y: 8, 14, 20
C. x: 1, 3, 5 | y: 6, 9, 12
D. x: 1, 3, 5 | y: 11, 14, 23
type: T8 — identify which table of values satisfies a linear inequality (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality
why_this_difficulty: Medium — substitute each (x, y) pair; table B uses exact boundary values that fail the strict inequality

distractor_rationales.B: The y-values equal exactly 3x + 5 for each row; equality does not satisfy the strict inequality y > 3x + 5
distractor_rationales.C: At x = 1: y = 6 is less than 3(1) + 5 = 8, not greater
distractor_rationales.D: At x = 3: y = 14 equals 3(3) + 5 = 14; equality does not satisfy the strict inequality

stem:
y > 5x − 3

A. x: 2, 4, 6 | y: 8, 18, 28
B. x: 2, 4, 6 | y: 7, 17, 27
C. x: 2, 4, 6 | y: 9, 17, 33
D. x: 2, 4, 6 | y: 12, 14, 29
type: T8 — identify the table where all (x, y) pairs satisfy a strict linear inequality (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality
why_this_difficulty: Medium — strict inequality; table B uses exact boundary values; must check all three rows per table

distractor_rationales.C: At x = 4: y = 17 equals 5(4) − 3 = 17; equality fails the strict inequality

stem:
y < x
x < 15
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given system of inequalities?
A. x: 12, 13, 14 | y: 11, 12, 13
B. x: 12, 13, 14 | y: 12, 13, 14
C. x: 12, 13, 14 | y: 13, 14, 15

type: T7 — identify the table satisfying a system of two inequalities (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given system of inequalities
why_this_difficulty: Medium — two simultaneous constraints: each x must be < 15 and each y must be strictly less than its x

distractor_rationales.B: In each row y = x, which fails the strict inequality y < x
distractor_rationales.C: In each row y > x, which fails y < x

stem:
An employee's total annual compensation consists of a base salary of b dollars plus a bonus equal to 8% of total sales made during the year. This year, the employee's goal is for the total compensation to be at least 2 times and at most 3 times the base salary. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible values of total sales s, in dollars, the employee must make to meet this goal?
A. b ≤ s ≤ 2b
B. (b/0.08) ≤ s ≤ (2b/0.08)
C. 2b ≤ s ≤ 3b
D. (2b/0.08) ≤ s ≤ (3b/0.08)
type: T2 — compound inequality requiring algebraic manipulation to isolate a commission variable (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: plus a bonus equal to ... % of total sales
at least ... times and at most ... times the base salary
all possible values of total sales s
why_this_difficulty: Hard — set up 2b ≤ b + 0.08s ≤ 3b; subtract b; divide by 0.08 to isolate s

distractor_rationales.A: Student subtracted b from the compensation range endpoints (2b − b = b and 3b − b = 2b) but forgot to divide by 0.08
distractor_rationales.C: Student used the total compensation range (2b to 3b) directly as the range for s, skipping the base salary subtraction
distractor_rationales.D: Student divided the compensation range (2b and 3b) by 0.08 without first subtracting the base salary

stem:
Two sides of a triangle have lengths 7 and 11. Which inequality represents all possible values of the third side x?
A. x < 18
B. x > 18
C. 4 < x < 18
D. x < 4 or x > 18
type: T2 — apply the triangle inequality theorem to write a compound inequality (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: which inequality represents all possible values of the third side
why_this_difficulty: Hard — triangle inequality: each side < sum and > difference of the other two; 7 + 11 = 18 and 11 − 7 = 4 give 4 < x < 18

distractor_rationales.A: Student applied only the upper bound (x < 7 + 11 = 18), ignoring the lower bound
distractor_rationales.B: Student reversed the upper bound direction — x must be less than 18, not greater
distractor_rationales.D: Student wrote the region outside the valid range instead of inside it

stem:
A school needs to purchase the same calculator for each of 48 students. The total budget is $2,400, which includes a 5% sales tax. Which of the following is closest to the maximum possible price per calculator, before sales tax, based on this budget?
A. $43.27
B. $47.62
C. $50.00
D. $52.63
type: T4 — find maximum unit price from a total budget that includes sales tax (MCQ)
sat_key_phrases: maximum possible price per calculator, before sales tax
why_this_difficulty: Hard — set up 48 × 1.05 × p ≤ 2,400; must apply the tax multiplier before dividing; p ≤ 2,400/50.4 ≈ 47.62

distractor_rationales.A: Student used an incorrect tax multiplier of 1.15 instead of 1.05 (2,400 ÷ (48 × 1.15) ≈ 43.48)
distractor_rationales.C: Student divided $2,400 by 48 without applying the 5% tax factor at all (2,400 ÷ 48 = 50.00)
distractor_rationales.D: Student subtracted the tax rate instead of adding it, using 0.95 as the multiplier (2,400 ÷ (48 × 0.95) ≈ 52.63)

stem: x is at most 4 less than 2 times y. If y = −3, what is the greatest possible value of x?
type: T6 — find max x from a two-variable bound when y is negative (SPR)
why_this_difficulty: Hard — translate to x ≤ 2y − 4; substitute y = −3 to get x ≤ 2(−3) − 4 = −10; a negative y produces a negative answer that is easy to miscalculate

stem:
y ≤ 3x + 1
y ≥ −x + 5

A. (−10, 0)
B. (0, −10)

sat_key_phrases: which ordered pair (x, y) is a solution to the given system of inequalities
why_this_difficulty: Hard — must substitute all four ordered pairs into both inequalities; only (10, 0) satisfies both

stem:
y > 9x − 12
